title: fix(types,plugin-dashboard): object-pivot refuses drillDown.mode on its prop type (objectui#10685, first half)
body:
Part of #10685
Clause-②: no — a per-block narrowing, as the ruling recorded for objectui#9002

## Status: the in-surface half, stopped at the claim's file surface

This PR carries the part of objectui#10685 that fits the claim's file surface (claim comment `5838176946`). The work follows the triage `5837818071`, which reuses objectui#9002's ruling `5643445104` (B, a per-block refusal). The `object-data-table` half needs two files the claim does not list, and the claim says to stop on a breach. So the first line is `Part of`, not a closing reference: merged alone, this PR leaves the data table's unread members, and its `target: 'navigate'`, accepted.

- **TypeScript door.** The data table's prop is anchored to `ObjectDataTableSchema`, declared in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`. `ObjectDataTable.schemaAnchor-6576.test.ts` pins `ObjectDataTableProps['schema']` as `Equal` to that type, so a per-block type cannot sit on the component prop without breaking the anchor. It has to replace `ObjectDataTableSchema.drillDown` in `objectql.ts`.
- **Zod door.** A runtime validator does read the data table's drill members: `objectui validate` runs `safeValidateSchema`, whose `object-data-table` arm types `drillDown` as `DrillDownConfigSchema`, in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` (probe below). The dispatch's condition for the zod door therefore applies: that door is narrowed too, not left accepted.

Neither file is in the surface. No open PR touches either region: PR objectui#8941 edits one comment in `objectql.ts`, far from both declarations, and no open PR touches `objectql.zod.ts`.

## What this does

- **`@object-ui/types`** adds `ObjectPivotDrillDownConfig` beside `ObjectMetricDrillDownConfig` in `data-display.ts`. It is `DrillDownConfig` plus a `mode?: never` tombstone in the #10681 idiom (a `REFUSED BY NAME` docblock and `@deprecated`, naming `object-data-table` as the block that reads `mode`). It is exported on the root entry and on the `@object-ui/types/data-display` subpath.
- **The `DrillDownConfig.mode` docblock** no longer names charts, pivot tables and metric cards as its users. None of them reads it. It names only `object-data-table`, and says what each value does there. `'filter'` turns the table's row drill off, which is the behaviour `ObjectDataTable.drill.test.tsx` already pins ("ignores filter-mode drill on a record table").
- **`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`**: `ObjectPivotTableProps.schema` gains `drillDown?: ObjectPivotDrillDownConfig` beside the members it already declares locally (`objectName`, `filter`, the `dataProvider` tombstone). The component's reads now go through that type: `schema.drillDown` replaces `(schema as any).drillDown`, and `drillDown?.report` replaces `(drillDown as any)?.report`.
- **`object-chart`: no type change** (see H4).
- **Pins**: `drill-down-per-block-10685.test.ts` in `@object-ui/types` has one `describe` per block, and `ObjectPivotTable.drillDownRefusal-10685.test.tsx` in `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` pins the published component's prop.
- **Changeset** `10685-drilldown-per-block.md`: `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`, both `patch`. It says the refusal is at the TypeScript door only, because `object-pivot` has no zod mirror.
- **H6**: `.changeset/7352-drill-down-config-mirror.md` said `mode` and `report` are "live keys on the table / pivot / metric widgets". That sentence is now scoped "at this change", with a `⚠️ Dated note, 2026-09-25 … objectui#10685` after it. The frontmatter md5 is `ecedb10c5189b2c8841ea736b67c3cc6` both before and after. No doc or README lists `DrillDownConfig` members for these blocks: `git grep -l -E "drillDown|DrillDownConfig"` over `content` and `packages/*/README.md` returns nothing, while the control word `object-chart` returns a hit in `content`.

## H1: the table, re-measured per block at `bc97f9247`

Two instruments, neither committed:

- **Runtime probe.** A scratch vitest file renders the real block and varies one member at a time against a control. It compares the rendered DOM after the drill click (with generated ids normalised), the data source calls and the host `openRecordList` calls. Every combination runs with and without a `DrillNavigationProvider`, and for chart and pivot across `target` drawer, dialog and navigate. Positive controls (members that are read) must come out DIFFERENT, which proves the probe can see a difference. `maxRows` is not used as a control: the probe's drill lists are empty, so a page size has nothing to show.
- **Zod probe.** `tsx` over `packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts`, calling `safeValidateSchema`: the door `objectui validate` and `objectui check` use.

| block | member | runtime probe | zod door | reading |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `object-chart` | `mode` (`record`, `filter`) | identical to control, 12 of 12 | refused, `unrecognized_keys` naming `mode` | unread |
| `object-chart` | `report` (inline, named) | identical to control, 12 of 12 | refused, `unrecognized_keys` naming `report` | unread |
| `object-chart` | control: `title`, `filter` | differ wherever a drawer renders | accepted | read |
| `object-pivot` | `mode` (`record`, `filter`) | identical to control, 12 of 12 | no `object-pivot` arm: every node is refused at `type` | unread |
| `object-pivot` | control: `title`, `filter`, `report` | differ wherever a drawer renders | — | read |
| `object-data-table` | `filter` (plain, and `${event.rowKey}`) | identical, 4 of 4 | accepted | unread |
| `object-data-table` | `maxRows` | identical, 2 of 2 | accepted | unread |
| `object-data-table` | `report` (inline, named) | identical, 4 of 4 | accepted | unread |
| `object-data-table` | `target: 'navigate'` | identical to the default drawer, 2 of 2, and `openRecordList` is never called | accepted | drawn as a drawer |
| `object-data-table` | control: `target: 'dialog'`, `title`, `columns`, `mode: 'filter'` | differ | invalid value on `enabled` refused | read |

Every path each block has was covered:

- `@object-ui/core`'s `isDrillEnabled`, `computeDrillFilter` and `resolveDrillTitle` read `enabled`, `filter` and `title` only.
- `DrillNavigationContext` carries one handler, `openRecordList(objectName, filter)`.
- `DrillDownDrawer` (pivot and metric) receives `target`, `columns`, `maxRows` and `report`.
- The chart builds its own drawer. Its inner table gets a hard-coded `{ enabled: true, mode: 'record', target: 'dialog' }`.
- The data table spreads its node, `drillDown` included, into the `data-table` it renders. That renderer (`packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx`) never names `drillDown`. `RecordDetailDrawer` takes `fields` (from `columns`), `title` and a two-armed `target`.

The card's per-block split holds. One reading in it does not: its runtime-door row (`ChartSchema.drillDown` is `DrillDownConfigSchema`) describes the plain `chart` node. `object-chart`'s own mirror is the spec's strict `ChartDrillDownSchema`, which already refuses `mode` and `report` (see H4).

## H2: can never honour, or not yet honoured (one line of evidence each)

- **`object-pivot` · `mode`: never.** Every pivot click point (a cell, a row or column header, a total) is an aggregated bucket, so the pivot always drills through. `mode` chooses drill-to-record for a clicked ROW, and a pivot has none. This is the metric's reasoning in `5643445104`, and it is refused here.
- **`object-chart` · `mode`, `report`: never, by the contract.** The chart's drill type is `@objectstack/spec`'s `ChartDrillDown`, the chart subset, which declares neither key. The spec's own schema refuses both by name, with guidance: "A chart segment is always an aggregate". Implementing `report` would widen past the spec. They are already refused, so nothing new is refused here.
- **`object-data-table` · `filter`, `maxRows`, `report`: never** (second half, not in this PR). All three configure a drilled LIST: the filter that scopes it, the rows it caps, or the report that replaces it. The data table drills to the RECORD it was clicked on, and `RecordDetailDrawer` lists nothing. Its `mode: 'filter'` arm is pinned as "ignored", so the block has no list-drill arm for these members to apply to. A table row that drills through to a list of some other object would need a drill-target member that `DrillDownConfig` does not have, so that is a new capability, not an unread member.
- **`object-data-table` · `target: 'navigate'`: refused, not honoured** (H3; second half).

## H3: `navigate` on the data table

`object-chart` honours `navigate` by calling `openRecordList(objectName, merged filter)`, which opens the object's LIST page scoped by the drill filter. `DrillNavigationContext` has no record-level handler, and the console's `useOpenRecordList` builds only the list route. The data table's click point is one record, so the list-page seam is the wrong destination for it. A "navigate to this record" arm needs a new host seam, which is not a small hunk. So the data table's type refuses `navigate` (`target?: 'drawer' | 'dialog'`), and an author gets a type error instead of a drawer. That lands with the second half.

## H4: where the shape differs from PR objectui#10681

- **`object-chart` keeps its spec-bound type.** `ObjectChartSchema.drillDown` is already a per-block shape, the spec's `ChartDrillDown`. `object-chart-undeclared-keys-8885.test.ts` pins it `Equal` to that symbol, under this repo's never-redefine rule. A fresh `mode` or `report` literal is already a compile error (an excess property on the fresh literal), and the zod mirror already refuses both by name. A tombstoned local type would unbind the declaration from the spec symbol. So this PR only pins the refused set: `report` at the TypeScript door had no pin before.
- **Registration sentences: none added, and none can be.** The `object-pivot` and `object-data-table` registrations in `plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx` advertise no `drillDown` input at all. Adding one would widen the designer palette, which is a shape decision. `object-chart`'s description lists exactly the six spec keys. `packages/plugin-charts/src/index.test.ts` ("describes the SIX keys the spec declares") asserts the description does not contain `mode` or `report`, so a sentence naming them would break a pin that exists to keep them out of the palette.
- **Zod door**: see the status section. The data table's door is real, and narrowing it is second-half work in `objectql.zod.ts`.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run type-check`, then plugin-dashboard's, then plugin-charts': `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` confirms each program compiles its pin, and plugin-dashboard's reads `packages/types/dist/data-display.d.ts`.

  - `check:control-bytes`: OK.
  - `changeset:check`: no `major`.
  - `check:changeset-claims`: 9 pending changesets name `data-display.ts` or `index.ts`. All 9 were read: they describe Gantt, breadcrumbs, the table toolbar, tree data, markdown, `wrapperClass`, `emptyAction`, list and timeline content, and table columns, and all stay true.
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `type-check:coverage`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:doc-types`.
  - `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the 7 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports` exited 1 on a prerequisite: 385 self-imports could not be judged because other packages' `dist/index.d.ts` files are not built. This diff edits no README and only adds a type export. Left to CI.
- ESLint was run on the 5 touched source and test files only, not the whole repo. The narrowing is safe for three reasons:
  - the config is the root `eslint.config.js`, and neither package has its own;
  - `--format json` reports 5 files, 0 errors and 38 warnings, all pre-existing `no-explicit-any`, none on an added line;
  - `--print-config` shows `parserOptions {}`, so there is no type-aware linting, and this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.

  The full `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- Serial check against PR objectui#10643. `origin/main` (`383a34f52`) and `claude/issue-10583-masked-cell-copy` (`4d341308a`) were fetched into private refs. `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 0 against both. Main moved in none of this PR's files, so no merge commit was needed.

## Red on base, then green on head (pins committed first; every restore proven by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

- **plugin-dashboard pin.** The HEAD pin was run against BASE `ObjectPivotTable.tsx` (blob `b37d1993ccb6` in place of HEAD `eeba53e84a43`). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exited 2 with two `TS2578 Unused '@ts-expect-error'` errors: the fresh `mode` literal and the handed-across shared config. It was then restored to HEAD `eeba53e84a43`, and exits 0 on HEAD.
- **types pin.** The HEAD pin was run against BASE `data-display.ts` and `index.ts`. It exited 2: `TS2724` (no exported member `ObjectPivotDrillDownConfig`) and two `TS2578` on the pivot refusals. Both files were restored to HEAD, and the pin exits 0 on HEAD. The chart half is green on base by design, because its refusal predates this card. Its proof is ablation B.
- **Ablation A**, through `ablation-replace.mjs`. The pivot tombstone `mode?: never;` became `mode?: DrillDownConfig['mode'];`: the anchor count went 1 to 0 and the blob `57be6df46ae1` to `09cf28ac1eba`. The types test program exited 2 with two `TS2578`, on the pivot lines only. Restored: the blob equals HEAD and the diff is empty.
- **Ablation B**, through `ablation-replace.mjs`. `ObjectChartSchema.drillDown?: ChartDrillDown;` became `DrillDownConfig`: the blob went `1dedf2768022` to `b5b8d1a8b059`. The program exited 2 with two `TS2578` on this PR's chart `mode` and `report` lines, plus the 8885 pins (`TS2344` on the spec-binding `Equal`, and `TS2578` on its `mode` line). Restored: the blob equals HEAD and the diff is empty.

Direction: red as predicted in every leg.

## Acceptance notes

- **`mode: 'filter'` on `object-data-table`** turns the row drill off, as `ObjectDataTable.drill.test.tsx` pins, instead of drilling through. The rewritten docblock now says so. This is value-level and outside the card's member set, so it is recorded here only.
- **`object-chart`, non-fresh values.** A value typed as the shared `DrillDownConfig` is still assignable to `ObjectChartSchema.drillDown`, because the spec type omits `mode` and `report` rather than tombstoning them. `DashboardRenderer` hands the chart `options.drillDown`, but `options` is typed as a record of string to `any`, so no producer in the tree hands a typed shared config across.
- **`maxRows`** reaches each drill list as the drill table's `pageSize` (`DrillDownDrawer` and `ObjectChart` both build `pageSize` from it). That is a page size, not the "Hard cap on rows fetched" the shared docblock promises. This is an observation outside this card.
- **The second half**, once the surface covers `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`:
  - `ObjectDataTableDrillDownConfig` (`filter`, `maxRows` and `report` as `?: never`; `target?: 'drawer' | 'dialog'`), wired at `ObjectDataTableSchema.drillDown`, with its zod twin wired at the mirror's `drillDown`;
  - the two 6576 anchor pins' `drillDown` rows, re-pointed at the new type;
  - the `DrillDownConfig` class docblock ("`target` is honoured by all of them") and the declared-keys pin comment ("`DrillDownDrawer.navigateOnly` for table / pivot / metric"), which are both false today for the data table;
  - a dated note on `.changeset/6576-widget-schema-anchors.md` ("`drillDown` (`DrillDownConfig`)").
